text:
Based on Good Housekeeping's July 2026 test of 15 speakers, the **JBL Grip** is the best pick for most people at the pool or beach.

**Top pick: [JBL Grip](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0FKVBT7NS), about $100**
- It has an IP68 rating, so it's sealed against dust and sand and can be submerged.
- Battery life is about 12 hours, and it weighs 0.85 lb.
- It's the size of a drink can and fits in a bag's bottle pocket.
- The tester said it has warm bass and was loud enough to compete with 30+ partygoers.
- One downside is that the mesh body collects dust and looks dirty after outdoor use.

**Other picks from the same test:**
- **Smallest: [Bose SoundLink Micro (2nd Gen)](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0FDLD34V5), about $129.**
  - It's IP67 with 12 hours of battery and weighs 0.7 lb. It has a strap you can clip to a backpack or cooler.
  - The mids and treble are clear, but the bass is weak and it isn't as loud as bigger speakers.
- **Best sound: [Bose SoundLink Plus](https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0GL8FBD85), about $269.**
  - It's IP67 with 20 hours of battery.
  - It has strong bass and stays clear at high volume. It weighs 3.29 lb, so it's much heavier than the others.

**What to look for:** Good Housekeeping recommends at least IPX7, which survives submersion, and IP6X if sand is a concern. It also suggests at least 12 hours of battery. All three picks charge by USB-C.

**Limits of this answer:**
- I only got usable content from the Good Housekeeping page.
- The RTINGS page loaded without its picks.
- The Tom's Guide page was too large for me to open, so I didn't read it.
- I didn't check the other review sites in your results.
- The prices are the ones Good Housekeeping listed, so check them before you buy.

I can also look for a louder party speaker or a cheaper option if you want one.

Sources: [Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/)
